newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months ended at a yield of 0.98/0.93 percent compared with Monday's yield of 1.03/0.98 percent.
One-year treasury bills ended at a yield of 1.49/1.44 percent against Monday's yield of 1.50/1.45 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.17/99.22 from Monday's close of S$99.15/99.20.
September 2001 was unchanged from Monday's close of S$97.35/97.40 and June 2003 unchanged at S$95.35/95.40.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Monday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
